postTitle: Income Replacement Ratio: How Much Income You Need in Retirement
topic: A pension reduces withdrawals only from the year it starts

caption.instagram:
You retire before your pension starts. Can it cut what you withdraw straight away?

No. In this example yearly spending is €55,000, including tax. Until the pension begins, investments cover all of it. From 67 the pension pays €25,000 a year, and only then do withdrawals fall to €30,000.

A common shortcut sizes the retirement pot as 25 times the gap between spending and pension income: here €750,000 instead of about €1.4 million. That shortcut assumes the income arrives from the first year of retirement. A pension that starts later leaves the earlier years to be funded in full, on top of that. The 25 times figure is itself a US rule of thumb that many treat as optimistic for long retirements.
